video.title: You Can Start This $1M/Yr Business With No Tools and No Crew

summary: Chris Koerner interviews Rex Lindsay, owner of Cozy Pros, a Phoenix home-performance business selling attic insulation removal/re-insulation, Aeroseal duct sealing, duct cleaning and air scrubbers, mostly via Facebook ads offering a free attic inspection. Rex says he moved from ~100 in-house employees to subcontracting nearly all installation work, with a project manager on site, citing lower insurance, equipment and quality-risk burden. He gives average ticket (~$10k), margin structure (~52% gross, 15-20% net target), lead cost (~$75) and ad return claims. Key takeaway: learn lead generation and sales, subcontract the labor, and use cheap front-end offers (duct cleaning, free inspection) to upsell large tickets.

speakers.name: Rex Lindsay
speakers.description: Owner of Cozy Pros, Phoenix home performance/insulation company

ideas.name: Subcontracted attic insulation + Aeroseal duct sealing package (Cozy Pros)
ideas.one_liner: Sell whole-attic insulation removal, sealing, R49 re-insulation and Aeroseal duct sealing via Facebook-ad free attic inspections, and subcontract all the installation work.
ideas.business_model: Per-job sales of installed packages; revenue minus subcontractor cost (~48-50%), commissions and ads
ideas.customer: Homeowners with older, under-insulated or leaky attics and ducts, in hot/cold climate metros (Phoenix, Dallas, Salt Lake)
ideas.problem: High energy bills, uncomfortable rooms, dusty or leaky ducts, degraded cellulose insulation
ideas.offer: Free attic inspection with infrared imaging, then remove old insulation, seal the attic, add R49 blown fiberglass, Aeroseal duct sealing, often duct cleaning, sometimes air scrubbers or HVAC units

pricing.notes: Uses consumer financing; cash value strips out financing fees. Utility rebates (e.g. SRP $400 duct sealing, $600 insulation) help sell.

acquisition_channels.details: Facebook video ads, often Rex on camera in an attic, pitching a free attic inspection with pain-point hooks; leads cost about $75 each; ad spend kept ~10% of revenue; ad return said to be 8-9x on bad months and 15x on good ones.

quote.text: our ads is really just to pitch a free attic inspection. Obviously, we're bringing up some of the pain points in our ads.
quote.speaker: Rex Lindsay

acquisition_channels.details: Commissioned in-home sales reps and project managers use infrared cameras to show leaking air; appointment setters and automations in High Level follow up leads.

ideas.delivery: Almost all work is subcontracted to small local insulation/duct companies who bring their own equipment and often buy materials (~48-50% of ticket goes to sub). Cozy Pros keeps a project manager as homeowner contact (about 60 jobs/month with one PM). Subs found via suppliers, Google, Facebook Marketplace and competing quotes.
unit_economics_claims: About 60 jobs a month in Phoenix with one project manager
Over $1M net profit per metro possible with subcontract model plus Facebook ads
ideas.startup_cost: Low with subcontracting; in-house route would need insulation machine $15-20k, removal machine ~$10k, duct machine $5-10k

acquisition.how: Paid Facebook ads are fully software-driven (creative, targeting, optimisation by agents); only on-camera video content needs a human occasionally.

onboarding.how: Lead intake and appointment setting can be automated via CRM, but an in-person inspection and sales presentation is needed.

delivery.how: Physical attic work by subcontractors; only subcontractor dispatch and scheduling could be tooled; a project manager is on site.

billing.how: Invoicing and financing links can be automated; commissions and sub payments need routine checks.

support.how: Warranty and quality issues involve site visits and sub management.

uk_applicability.notes: UK homes have different insulation norms (loft insulation, no widespread ducted AC), so Aeroseal duct sealing and Phoenix-style ducts largely do not apply. Loft insulation, ventilation or heat-pump related work is plausible but with different regulation, grants (ECO, etc.) and pricing.

risks: Sales rep reliance, in-person sales required

quotes.text: The fastest way in this business to cash flow and to start making some good healthy profits is to subcontract it.
quotes.speaker: Rex Lindsay

quotes.text: Our average ticket is right around 10 grand.
quotes.speaker: Rex Lindsay

ideas.name: Air scrubber installation and upsell
ideas.one_liner: Install plug-in HVAC air scrubbers (30-minute job) sold at $1,200 with ~$450 cost, with replacement cells every 2-3 years.
ideas.business_model: Product plus install sale with recurring cell replacement
ideas.customer: Homeowners with allergies, asthma, dust concerns
ideas.problem: Poor indoor air quality, allergens, pollen, viruses, mold
ideas.offer: HVAC-mounted ionising air purifier installed in the plenum

acquisition_channels.details: Currently an upsell during attic inspection or duct work; Rex thinks a standalone business could run on Facebook ads or door-to-door.

ideas.delivery: 30-minute install into the plenum with an outlet or adapter; homeowners could self-install.
unit_economics_claims: Rex says focusing could reach $1M a year

acquisition.how: Paid ads feasible; fear-based health sales may need a human call.

onboarding.how: Home visit needed to check install location.

delivery.how: Physical install in the plenum or attic.

support.how: Reorder reminders for cells can be automated.

uk_applicability.notes: Depends on ducted central HVAC, which is uncommon in UK homes.

risks: Efficacy and health claims may breach UK advertising rules

tools: Negative air machine with air whips

uk_applicability.notes: Ducted systems are uncommon in UK homes; commercial/ventilation duct cleaning exists.

tactics.name: Free attic inspection as ad hook
steps: Run Facebook video ads with the owner in an attic talking about pain points
Offer a free attic inspection as the call to action
Appointment setters book leads via High Level automations
Inspect with infrared cameras and show homeowners the images
Present a tailored package and add on air scrubbers or duct cleaning based on symptoms

quote.text: our ads are really just focused on providing a free attic inspection and once we do that then we kind of know the solution
quote.speaker: Rex Lindsay

tactics.name: Infrared imaging as sales visual
steps: Give every sales rep and project manager an infrared camera
Turn on the AC or heater on arrival
Capture images of ducts and attic leaks
Show the glowing leaks so homeowners see money burning

quote.text: show them the picture of like the glowing red and yellow and they're like oh my they just see like their money like burning up.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Find and manage subcontractors
steps: Ask equipment and material suppliers for recommended subs
Search Google, Facebook Marketplace for small local companies
Use competing customer quotes to identify cheaper subs
Vet several; expect early failures
Keep a project manager on site to control homeowner communication
Keep subs busy so they depend on you

quote.text: The best way to find really good subs is through the suppliers.
quote.speaker: Rex Lindsay

tactics.name: Self-liquidating cheap front-end offer
steps: Advertise a low-price duct cleaning offer that covers lead cost
Sell it over the phone
Upsell air scrubber, duct sealing or bigger jobs once on site

quote.text: you can come up with this like really good offer on the front end to bank on some of the upsells
quote.speaker: Rex Lindsay

tactics.name: Stack utility rebates
steps: Check local utility rebates for duct sealing and insulation
Include them in the quote to shorten payback

warnings.warning: Running everything in-house was costly: heavy equipment, ~100 employees, $15k/month rental repairs, higher liability.
Ice storms and weather can halt work in some markets like Dallas.

lessons.lesson: In home services, the money is in marketing and sales; labor can be rented via subcontractors.

quote.text: you need to learn Facebook ads, correct? Right.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Subcontracting moves equipment, repair and liability risk onto the sub and lowers capital needs.
Use a low-barrier front-end offer then upsell to grow ticket size.
Visual proof (thermal imaging) makes a data-driven sale to homeowners.
Choose extreme-weather markets for the strongest demand for comfort and efficiency work.
Sell the whole outcome (comfort, health, energy) rather than a single product, and sell the main course not an add-on.
Keep ad spend, commissions and overhead each near 10% to hit a 15-20% net target.
Recurring consumable replacement (air scrubber cells every 2-3 years) gives repeat touchpoints.

evidence_quality.rationale: First-hand operator giving specific margins, ticket sizes and process, but numbers are unverified and some claims (e.g. $1M air scrubber potential, $1M net per metro) are hypothetical or agreed leading questions.
evidence_quality.promotional_conflict: Host promotes TK Owners community and a Beehiiv sponsor; guest promotes his own Cozy Pros business and CRM.
